### Observed differences

- In the later window, A04 appears in about 37 in 100 traces, down from about 76 in 100, and its mean occurrences per trace fall from about 0.87 to 0.44 [OCC001].
- In the later window, A14 usually continues without A04: about 65 in 100 of A14's outgoing transitions go to A15 (before about 29 in 100) and about 28 in 100 go to A04 (before about 70 in 100), and A14 occurs without A04 in about 64 in 100 traces versus about 25 in 100 before. When A04 does run, its outgoing mix stays dominated by A15, though less strongly (about 83 in 100 before, 65 in 100 after) [DIR003, REL001, DIR002].
- In the later window, the group A19, A20, A25, A26 keeps broadly similar participation (between about 22 and 30 in 100 traces in both windows) but sits later in the case: mean event position rises from about one-third to about one-half of the trace for all four activities (A25 median 0.32 to 0.61) [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004].
- In the later window, each of A19, A20, A25 and A26 leads mainly to A29 and A33 (about 70-80 in 100 of outgoing transitions combined), where before each led to A27 in roughly 88-96 in 100 cases; A27 now receives at most about 25 in 100 from these activities [DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007].
- Order relative to A27/A28 reverses in the later window: A20 precedes A27 in about 22 in 100 traces before and about 7 in 100 after, while A27 precedes A20 in about 22 in 100 after (about 0.5 in 100 before); A19 and A25 show the same reversal against A27 and A28 [REL013, REL012, REL014, REL015, REL016].
- In the later window, the group's neighbours change: A46 now leads to A27 in about 67 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (before about 0.5 in 100, with about 22-26 in 100 each to A19/A20/A25/A26), while A28 and A29 now lead to A19/A20/A25/A26 in roughly 40 in 100 of their outgoing transitions, mostly 1-2 steps away (before almost only A29 and A33 respectively); A28-to-A33 distances stretch from 2 steps in about 96 in 100 cases to 3 steps in about 76 in 100 [DIR010, DIR008, DIR009, LAG012, LAG013, LAG015, LAG020].
- Two weaker signals in the later window: A10 participation rises from about 7 to 16 in 100 traces, and A02's outgoing mix appears completely turned over, but both rest on few observations (A10: 14 versus 32 traces; A02: 12 versus 40 outgoing transitions) [OCC002, DIR001].

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility of a structural change with two faces. First, A04 is not executed in about 63 in 100 later cases (versus about 24 in 100 before), and A14 typically proceeds directly to A15 instead of through A04, while A04's own follow-up behaviour when it runs is largely retained [OCC001, DIR003, REL001, DIR002]. Second, the sequence A19, A20, A25, A26 is placed later in the case: it is now reached mainly from A28/A29 and leads on to A29/A33, whereas before it was reached after A46 and led to A27, and it now follows A27/A28 in the trace order instead of preceding them; the participation, order, routing, position and distance items show this directly and consistently, and every listed difference is larger than in about 199 of 200 random re-splits of the pooled windows [DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, LAG015, LAG020].

The evidence cannot rule out that the later window simply contains more of a variant without A04 and with the A19/A20/A25/A26 group in its later position — a shift in the variant mix between two finite 200-trace samples rather than a modification of the process itself — although the size and consistency of the shifts make pure sampling noise an unlikely full explanation. The items are also not independent confirmations: the A04 relations largely re-express the participation drop, and the group's routing, order, position and distance items describe one and the same move; several LAG profiles for the new adjacencies rest on a single before-window observation, and the evidence does not show whether the two shifts are one coordinated restructuring or two separate ones [REL001, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010, LAG011, LAG012, LAG013, LAG016].
